CVIAF — merged clean-null FPR ledger

What the evaluator wrote, and what this page recomputes from the same bytes

Every row below was recomputed in this page from the embedded per-model scores, using the committed split seed and a Wilson interval. A disagreement would have failed the build - if you see one, that is a bug, not a rounding note. Thresholds come from the calibration half's negatives only; the rate is measured on the evaluation half, which never contributed to the threshold.

How this population was assembled

Move the threshold yourself

This is the falsification tool. Pick a signal and a population, drag the threshold, and watch the rate follow. The committed operating point is marked; reset returns to it. Nothing here is simulated - it is the same 56,627 scored models the report is built from.

Signal distribution on this population

Left of the line is the calibration half (used to choose the threshold), right is the held-out half. A signal whose clean scores pile up at 1.0 cannot produce a separation, which is the degeneracy the headline table reports rather than hides.

What the 5% false-alarm budget actually buys

These are attacked variants derived from models that are already in the clean population above - weight-space tampering only (head noise and structural pruning), no retraining, no new data. They were scored through the same adapter against the same pinned reference, and then judged at the thresholds the FPR half already chose. Nothing here recalibrated anything: the clean ledger and its thresholds are untouched, and this is a separate receipt.

Per attack class

Two classes, because a single class cannot tell a rule that misses weak attacks from one that misses all of them. Attack severity varies widely within a class - some head tampers improve f1, because zero-mean noise on a trained head is closer to regularisation than to sabotage.

Per-source breakdown at the committed threshold

Eleven shards, three machines. A pooled rate can hide a source that behaves differently, so the per-shard rate is printed beside it - and a shard whose interval excludes the pooled rate is flagged rather than averaged away.

Symbols

Click a row to load that shard into the explorer as a population.

The split is a free parameter too

The threshold and the evaluation half both come from a deterministic permutation seeded by a single integer. Re-run with a different seed and the headline moves by a few thousandths. That spread is the honest resolution of this measurement, and it is printed here rather than buried - a single split seed quoted alone would overstate the precision.
